title: Artist in residence and teaching
summary: He fears the traps of academia; Benny Carter's semester.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Have you ever gotten any offers for any artist in residence type thing?

That might have been good, depending how it's done, but I've always been afraid of getting in a trap that I couldn't get out of, because I've gotten myself in some traps. I've managed to squirm out of them one way or another, but no, I haven't.
That would depend on circumstances; where it was, what the conditions would be. It's not likely to happen, I'm over age now. I don't think they can even hire people sixty five.
He was there for a limited--he did a semester--
He came in as a guest, but he isn't on the faculty, though.
That's different from what you said the other day. I thought he was too.
He taught for a while. He was teaching courses and he was rehearsing the band, and he was there for a semester at a time. That was fairly recently.
I thought he was still there.
No, he did it for a limited amount of time.
Did he stop it or did they?
I think it was prearranged that he would do it for X amount of time, before he went in. At the time I think he still had commitments on the coast that he knew he was going to have.

One of the traps when you do something like that is you cut yourself off from what you have, and then everyone forgets, and all of a sudden you have nothing, and none of us are in a position to weather that sort of thing. It gets worse as you get older; you'd think it got better, but it doesn't, it gets worse. The possibility is no longer there; when you're younger, you have time and then at one point there isn't.
It would be nice maybe in your case just if you got in a university situation for a semester where you could--for one thing, if you wanted to play some of that Sauter-Finegan music, you'd have a--
